title: Field observations: GPU + Kubernetes compatibility playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a field-first playbook containing observational notes, a compact compatibility matrix, quick validation steps, and Terraform module hints for on-prem/VPC private deployments. The doc is intended to capture real cluster outcomes from QA runs and early customer upgrades (alpha/beta), so it mixes bullet observations, repro snippets, and recommended mitigations.

Scope:
- Kubernetes control plane and kubelet versions tested on customer clusters and lab rigs.
- NVIDIA driver releases and CUDA toolkits observed in the field.
- NCCL versions and common failure modes under multi-GPU workloads.
- Container runtime variants (containerd vs docker-shim) and OCI image tags.
- Terraform module variables and quick checks for driver/cuda ties.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Most customer regressions come from mismatched driver <-> kernel combos or outdated NCCL with newer CUDA release.
- containerd + nvidia-container-toolkit is most stable in our tests; docker-shim shows more transient binding races during node restart.
- Keep a narrow compatibility window: officially support NVIDIA drivers + CUDA that match the model quantization/Perf path (e.g., 525.x + CUDA 11.8 for Ampere 80GB variants).
- Add preflight checks in Terraform module to prevent applying incompatible driver versions in upgrade playbooks.

Observed compatibility matrix (field data; rows show scenarios we ran in lab or saw from customers):

K8s Version | Linux Kernel | NVIDIA Driver | CUDA | NCCL | Container Runtime | Observed Result | Recommended action
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1.26.3      | 5.15         | 525.116.04    | 11.8 | 2.16 | containerd        | PASS (stable)    | baseline config, mark as compatible
1.25.7      | 5.10         | 470.199.02    | 11.4 | 2.7  | docker (shim)     | WARNING (OOM under burst) | increase GPU cgroup limits, prefer containerd
1.27.1      | 6.1          | 535.86.10     | 12.1 | 2.18 | containerd        | FAIL (nvml init race on reboot) | pin driver or update kubelet kubelet-cgroup settings; restart ordering fix
1.24.9      | 5.4          | 470.199.02    | 10.2 | 2.6  | containerd        | PASS (but NCCL perf low) | consider NCCL 2.9+ backport or avoid chain all-reduce workloads
1.26.0      | 5.15         | 470.199.02    | 11.8 | 2.15 | containerd        | PARTIAL (cuda drivers mismatch warnings) | replace driver with 525.x for CUDA 11.8 images or use CUDA 11.4 images
1.27.1      | 6.1          | 535.86.10     | 12.1 | 2.12 | docker (shim)     | FAIL (NCCL COMM errors under multi-pod) | upgrade NCCL to 2.18+ or isolate via network policy

Notes on the matrix: these are condensed notes from multiple runs. The key patterns: kernel version matters for driver ABI, NCCL minor version interacts with network stack (RoCE/ethernet), and container runtime influences device plugin lifecycle stability.

Common failure modes (field examples) and repro steps:
- NVML init race on node reboot
  - Symptoms: GPU plugin reports "device not found" for 30-120s after kubelet restart; pods in CrashLoop with "nvidia-smi timed out" logs.
  - Repro: rapid drain + Cordon + reboot sequence while GPU pods pinned with local PVs.
  - Observed root cause: NVIDIA modules not loaded before kubelet starts (init ordering).
  - Quick mitigations: systemd drop-in to delay kubelet until nvidia-modprobe returns success; add node-preflight check in Terraform to test modprobe.

- NCCL COMM errors during multi-pod all-reduce
  - Symptoms: intermittent NCCL timeout errors, degraded throughput, occasional hangs.
  - Repro: distributed all-reduce on 8xA100 under high network saturation across hosts.
  - Observed root cause: incompatible NCCL used with particular network driver or missing GID/MTU tuning on fabric.
  - Mitigation: pin to NCCL 2.18+ for 12.x CUDA; enforce MTU/GID profile in cluster bootstrap; add perf test (iperf + nccl-tests) during upgrade canary.

- OOMs from sidecar containers during burst tokenization jobs
  - Symptoms: sidecars killed, GPU containers keep running but job fails due to orchestration loops.
  - Repro: high concurrency tokenization with batch size bursts.
  - Observed root cause: default kubelet cgroup resources low on some Ubuntu LTS kernels.
  - Mitigation: bump system reserved/cgroup settings in node bootstrap and document in terraform module variables.

Validation checklist (smoke + regression harness for upgrades):
1) Node preflight (agent runs on baremetal): kernel version, modprobe nvidia, nvidia-smi works, driver matches kernel ABI.
2) Container runtime probe: start a test image with nvidia runtime, run a small GPU compute (vector add) within container and validate results.
3) NCCL probe: run nccl-tests/all_reduce on 2 hosts with representative MTU/roce config.
4) K8s lifecycle probe: cordon & drain node, restart kubelet, ensure GPU pods reschedule within SLO.
5) Terraform dry-run: validate tfvars constraints and run 'plan' with preflight checks that prevent driver mismatch.
6) Canary rollout: 5% nodes with new driver/CUDA and run full regression harness for 24h before 100% rollout.

Terraform module notes and snippets (practical):
- Recommend adding a preflight null_resource that executes a user data script to check driver <-> kernel ABI. If check fails, module should fail early.
- Example constraint (policy): prevent driver_version < 510 when cuda_version >= 11.8.
- Quick variable schema suggestion (strings):
  - gpu_driver_version: string
  - cuda_version: string
  - nccl_version: string
  - prefer_container_runtime: string (containerd|docker)

Example preflight shell (for null_resource local-exec):
#!/bin/bash
set -e
KVER=$(uname -r)
DRIVER=$(modinfo nvidia | grep -E '^version:' | head -n1 | awk '{print $2}')
if [[ -z "$DRIVER" ]]; then echo "NO_DRIVER"; exit 2; fi
# crude mapping check (replace with a lookup table in module)
if [[ "$DRIVER" < "510" && "${var.cuda_version}" > "11.4" ]]; then
  echo "INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER"
  exit 3
fi
echo "PREFLIGHT_OK"

Operational rollout playbook (short):
- Phase 0: Preflight & dry-run (Terraform plan + node preflight).
- Phase 1: Apply to canary nodes (5%), run validation harness (72 hours recommended for heavy NCCL workloads).
- Phase 2: Roll forward 20% increments with monitoring thresholds (NCCL error rate, pod restart count, GPU utilization drift).
- Phase 3: Full rollout + postmortem collection if errors exceed thresholds.
- Rollback: maintain a driver rollback package and a live inventory of nodes that can be returned to previous driver image via an automated Kexec container or imaging pipeline.

Field tips and heuristics (learned):
- Keep the driver and CUDA mapping table as code in the Terraform module (small JSON or map), not just in docs.
- Prefer containerd + nvidia-container-toolkit on modern images; explicitly test docker shim only if a customer requires it.
- NCCL minor upgrades are low-risk only if kernel+driver are current. When in doubt, stage NCCL upgrade after driver upgrade.
- Record timestamps of kernel ABI changes for each node image; this helps root-cause when drivers appear incompatible.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want to gate terraform apply with an automated lab run (sandbox cluster) that validates canary images before customer apply? Pros/cons in linked confluence page.
- Should the module include an enforced image list for CUDA base images to reduce accidental mismatch?
- Decide on a strict supported matrix (narrow) vs soft recommendations (wider) for public docs.

Appendix: raw example logs (condensed)
[2026-02-21 03:12:07] kubelet: failed to get device plugin: nvidia: device not found
[2026-02-21 03:12:34] kernel: nvidia: module not inserted: unresolved symbol error
[2026-02-21 04:02:11] nccl: NCCL WARN Connect: Timeout waiting for rank 3

- Priya: add containerd test case to our regression harness and schedule weekly runs against latest drivers.
